name: The Carenage
tagline: The horseshoe harbour at the centre of everything
description: The inner harbour of St George's, a curve of pastel warehouses and shipping offices around the water with Fort George on the headland above. It is the most photographed view in Grenada and the working heart of the capital.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to be in the capital rather than at the beach
pros: The most beautiful harbour in the Eastern Caribbean
Market, banks and ferries all walkable
Fort George and the Sendall Tunnel

name: Grand Anse
tagline: Three kilometres of white sand ten minutes from town
description: The long crescent of beach south of the capital, with hotels and apartments along it, a craft market at one end and minibuses running to St George's constantly. It is where most visitors and long-stay residents base themselves.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the beach and easy access to the capital
pros: One of the finest beaches in the Caribbean
Ten minutes to St George's by minibus
cons: Busy when cruise ships are in

name: Lance aux Epines
tagline: The southern peninsula, quiet and expensive
description: A residential peninsula at the southern tip of the island with villas, a marina at Prickly Bay and several small beaches. It is where much of the yachting and long-term expatriate population lives, and it is calm to the point of soporific.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting quiet, a marina and villa-style housing
pros: Prickly Bay marina and the yachting community
Several small beaches within walking distance
cons: The most expensive part of Grenada
Almost nothing happens in the evening

name: Morne Rouge
tagline: The quieter bay next to Grand Anse
description: A small sheltered bay just south of Grand Anse, separated by a headland, with calmer water, fewer people and a handful of restaurants and guesthouses. It offers most of Grand Anse's convenience with considerably less of its traffic.
bestFor: Anyone who wants Grand Anse's location without its crowds
pros: Calmest swimming water on the south coast
Quieter than Grand Anse next door
Walking distance to Grand Anse amenities
cons: Still needs transport into St George's

name: Gouyave
tagline: The fishing town where the nutmeg is processed
description: A working fishing town on the west coast, half an hour north of the capital, with the island's main nutmeg processing station where the work is still done by hand, and Fish Friday, a weekly street food night that fills the whole town.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a genuinely local town at local prices
pros: The cheapest rents on the west coast
The nutmeg station and a real working harbour
cons: The beach here is not the island's best
